BIBLIOGRAPHIC RECORD

Samuel Waddington, comp.  The Sonnets of Europe.  1888.

On a Nun

Vittorelli

Translated by Lord Byron
O
F
 two fair virgins, modest, though admired,
Heaven made us happy; and now, wretched sires,
Heaven for a nobler doom their worth desires,
And gazing upon 
either, both
 required.
Mine, while the torch of Hymen newly fired
Becomes extinguish’d, soon—too soon—expires:
But thine, within the closing grate retired,
Eternal captive, to her God aspires.
But 
thou,
 at least, from out the jealous door,
Which shuts between your never-meeting eyes,
May’st hear her sweet and pious voice once more:
I to the marble, where 
my
 daughter lies,
Rush,—the swoln flood of bitterness I pour,
And knock, and knock, and knock—but none replies.
